model_A1_A6_and_reduced_problem.statement: A1--A6 fix the technology, costs, binary activity and restart state, discounting and information, matched one-period shocks, and positive normal profit; after conditional input optimization the paper studies the displayed infinite-horizon reduced activity problem.
model_A1_A6_and_reduced_problem.source_note: Composite governing-model prerequisite for all six numbered claims; it also makes the full-program to reduced-program coverage boundary visible.

suspension_extension_model.statement: The robustness extension adds a date-zero suspension action that produces zero, pays h instead of operating overhead, preserves the organization, and permits costless resumption at date one.
suspension_extension_model.source_note: The action and value semantics embedded inside Proposition 3's source presentation.

fixed_cohort_aggregation.statement: The corollary defines matched fixed-cohort totals as Y_t^j=B+N y_t^j and uses the same positive population divisor in every per-capita path.
fixed_cohort_aggregation.source_note: Aggregation and common-population definitions embedded in Corollary 1.

lemma1_operating_optimum.statement: Lemma 1: conditional on operating at s>0 under A1--A2, the unique global input optimum satisfies the displayed FOC, optimizer, output, and profit formulas, independently of restart cost.

lemma2_restored_state_values_and_delays.statement: Lemma 2: V is the active restored value, W=max(V-kappa,0) is the inactive value; restart or permanent inactivity is uniquely optimal on the strict sides, while every delay and never restarting tie at equality.
lemma2_restored_state_values_and_delays.source_note: Complete source presentation of Lemma 2, including arbitrary delayed restart.

proposition1_persistent_strict_asymmetry.statement: Proposition 1: under positive normal profit, negative adverse continuation value, and kappa>V, adverse closure is permanent and unique, normal and favorable firms remain active, losses strictly exceed gains at every date, while the free-restart adverse firm reopens at date one and later gaps vanish.
proposition1_persistent_strict_asymmetry.source_note: Complete source presentation of Proposition 1, including the free-restart baseline.

proposition2_complete_closure_threshold.statement: Proposition 2: the adverse closure threshold is an iff with the displayed damage term, with reverse and equality cases, post-restoration behavior for all kappa/V regions, and weak loss-gain asymmetry under any optimal tie selection.

proposition3_cheap_suspension.statement: Proposition 3: under Proposition 1's strict conditions and 0<=h<beta V, the adverse firm uniquely suspends and resumes at date one, normal and favorable firms operate, the impact loss is q0, and all later loss and gain vanish.
proposition3_cheap_suspension.source_note: Complete source presentation of Proposition 3 and its date-zero suspension action.

corollary1_positive_totals_and_logs.statement: Corollary 1: common positive B and N make all three cohort totals positive and the adverse log loss strictly exceed the favorable log gain at every date; the comparison also holds for common-population per-capita totals.

source_named_result_inventory_review.method: Read the complete pinned TeX and rendered eight-page PDF; independently enumerated every numbered lemma, proposition, and corollary plus the governing A1--A6 model and reduced activity problem; cross-checked the six named environments with the repository extractor.

source_region_partition.method: The paper has no appendix or supplement; the complete 198-line canonical TeX is one main-text region.
